summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted with nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and epigastric pain, two days after a prior discharge for similar symptoms. He has a history of alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis, status post RFA and TACE for liver lesions, and is awaiting transplant. Workup revealed moderate fecal loading on CT, but no acute abdominal process. An upper endoscopy showed a friable 2 cm duodenal polyp with an ulcer, consistent with chronic duodenitis, but no bleeding; biopsy was deferred due to bleeding risk. A gastric emptying study demonstrated moderately delayed emptying, explaining persistent nausea. Iron supplements were discontinued as a potential contributor to symptoms. Metabolic alkalosis from vomiting resolved with supportive care. Diuretics were held initially for hypovolemia and restarted at discharge with reduced spironolactone. He improved on a gentle diet, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.
problems: Duodenal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
Benign neoplasm of duodenum, jejunum, and ileum
Malignant neoplasm of liver, not specified as primary or secondary
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, in remission
